needs_review: db_query.ts does not call enableAudit() when wiki.config.yaml sets audit.enabled=true; the assertion about 'no connect/pool_created/query_executed audit events' is vacuously satisfied rather than positively proved. Timing+stderr evidence still carries the assertion.
workarounds: Executor saved a 0-byte audit.jsonl placeholder in outputs/ to make proof-of-absence explicit, since the CLI never created the file.

suggestions.assertion: No audit event of type 'connect', 'pool_created', or 'query_executed' is written for env=production - a clean run contains only the policy_deny entry
suggestions.reason: This assertion is currently satisfied vacuously because db_query.ts does not wire audit from wiki.config.yaml. A skill that silently skipped the policy gate and only failed at DNS would also produce zero audit events (since audit is never enabled). The assertion text says 'a clean run contains only the policy_deny entry' - that positive-presence half is not actually verifiable today. Tighten by either (a) adding the enableAudit wiring first as a prerequisite and asserting exactly one policy_deny entry and zero of the other three types, or (b) replacing the audit check with a stronger behavioral proof (e.g., assert that the process never opened a socket - can be checked with DTrace/strace or by blocking outbound DNS at the resolver level).

suggestions.assertion: Exit code is non-zero and distinguishes policy deny from a generic error
suggestions.reason: The current exit code is 1, which is the same as any generic node error. The assertion passes because the stdout JSON carries 'status':'denied' as a parseable marker, but a caller using only $? could not distinguish a policy deny from a crash. If distinguishing exit codes matters operationally, consider requiring a dedicated exit code (e.g., 2 for policy_deny, 1 for runtime error).

No assertion verifies that the SQL was never sent to any driver / pool even at the in-process level. A stronger behavioral assertion would spy on the driver's execute/executeReadAsync and require call_count == 0 - this would fail closed if a future refactor accidentally reorders the policy check after pool creation. The 50ms wall-time proxy catches the DNS/TCP case but not an in-process connection-string validation step.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are substantially stronger than iteration-2 (end-to-end CLI, wall time, stderr, exit code all tested), but the audit-event assertion is undermined by a known wiring gap. Consider either gating this eval on the enableAudit wiring landing, or pivoting the audit assertion to a direct behavioral check (driver.execute spy or syscall trace).
